interpretation: Strong universality turns approximation into a zero-production mechanism because dropping the nonvanishing condition permits a target with a zero. Uniform approximation to s-sigma_0 on a small disk lets Rouche transfer its single zero to phi(s+i tau). This local transfer alone does not prove the stated global CT bound: if the successful shifts in [delta,T-delta] have measure at least cT, each resulting source zero can account for shifts only in an interval of length at most 2delta around its imaginary part, so covering the successful-shift set forces at least cT/(2delta) distinct zeros (up to fixed endpoint losses). The mechanism yields a linear lower bound inside the strong-universality region, not zero locations or the unresolved algebraic-irrational Hurwitz case.
source_support: Theorem 10 states strong universality for Hurwitz zeta when alpha is transcendental or rational other than 1 and 1/2, supported respectively by Q-linear independence of log(n+alpha) and reduction to joint Dirichlet L-function universality; it explicitly leaves algebraic irrational alpha open. Theorem 11 chooses f(s)=s-sigma_0, obtains a positive-lower-density set of shifts, and uses Rouche on a small disk to produce a source zero near sigma_0+i tau. Corollary 1 records the resulting linear zero bounds for the stated Hurwitz cases.
nonparaphrase_operation: The revision separates two proof burdens that the terse source presentation runs together: topological stability transfers one target zero for each successful shift, while a bounded-overlap covering in the shift variable converts positive lower density into a linear number of distinct source zeros. It also identifies the representational gain of zero-bearing targets and the limitation that the frequency argument covers only the stated parameter classes and strip.

The exact rational decomposition formula is treated as formula-sensitive and is not reconstructed beyond the source's stated reduction.
